quantities.joint: J-truth: truth labels, uniform budget and BSGS equations

scope.model_provenance: Requested review-adversarial/xhigh, fresh independent session. Serving model is unverified; no probe executed or invented.
scope.metadata_exposure: Original frozen protocol/spec/trial and permitted contracts contain historical metadata/formulas/review references; this is not a sanitized tree. Referenced historical reports and source paths were not opened.
scope.literature_scope_and_gap: Only the exhaustive phase1 allowlist was read. Original protocol literature entries were inspected as historical metadata; their referenced reports/papers were not opened. No novelty, prior-work completeness or external authority claim. Elementary group/combinatorial derivations below stand on stated assumptions.

assumptions.curve: E/F_p: v^2=u^3+A*u+B, p>3 prime, 4*A^3+27*B^2 != 0 mod p.
assumptions.subgroup: G != O has exact odd prime order r, and Q != O belongs to <G>. Write Q=[z]G with canonical scalar 1<=z<=r-1.
assumptions.point_and_scalar_notation: u,v denote point coordinates; z denotes a discrete-log scalar. A point x-coordinate does not determine z.
not_assumed: No half-truth/candidate correlation, scalar ordering from coordinates, independent nested cells, runtime law, speedup, or native cost qualification.

group_and_sign.public_equation: Accept a canonical nonzero witness z only after independent on-curve/subgroup checks and [z]G=Q. Since ord(G)=r, equality holds iff witnesses agree modulo r.
group_and_sign.negation: -(u,v)=(u,-v mod p); [r-z]G=-Q. Q and -Q share u and normally differ in v. In an odd-order subgroup no nonidentity point equals its negative.
group_and_sign.identity_boundary: [0]G=O; it cannot solve a nonidentity Q. Integers outside [0,r-1] may represent residues, but must be separately rejected or explicitly normalized according to a documented input contract; they must never inflate distinct legal M.
group_and_sign.order_certificate: For prime r, G!=O and [r]G=O imply exact order r. Independent same-curve orbit enumeration can additionally verify no early repeat, closure at r, and retained point/log assignments without a new scientific trial.

half_truth.sealed_auditor_convention: H_G([k]G)=+1 for 1<=k<r/2, -1 for r/2<k<=r-1; H_G(O)=undefined. Equivalently lower half k<=floor(r/2) is +1.
half_truth.anchors_and_sign: H_G(G)=+1; H_G(-G)=-1; H_G(-R)=-H_G(R) on nonidentity points. H is not geometric y-sign or a function of the point x-coordinate alone.
half_truth.binary_encoding: Set b_G(R)=(1-H_G(R))/2: lower=0, upper=1. A producer may encode these two values differently, but the mapping must be stated from its explicit convention and anchors rather than fitted to outcomes.
half_truth.calibration_truth: For defined candidate label ell in {-1,+1}, score=ell*H_G(R); correct +1, wrong -1, undefined 0. Unconditional mean=(correct-wrong)/all_draws; undefined draws remain in denominator.
half_truth.phase1_specification_gap: The allowed statement/protocol/spec/trial name half-truth/list semantics but do not explicitly give the exact retained label bit encoding or doubling direction. The anchored mathematical convention and forward-doubling interval below are independently sealed; phase2 must disclose the actual explicit encoding/indexing and check its exact algebraic correspondence. No retained label result is inferred now.

blinding_and_unblinding.domain: a,b are nonzero modulo prime r; P=[a]G, Qprime=[b]Q, Q=[z]G.
blinding_and_unblinding.derivation: [k]P=Qprime iff a*k=b*z mod r, hence k=b*a^-1*z mod r and z=a*b^-1*k mod r.
blinding_and_unblinding.verification: Independently verify both [k]P=Qprime and [z]G=Q. Neither metadata equality nor successful conversion without these equations is enough. Retain costs of both checks and conversion as separate dimensions.
blinding_and_unblinding.sign_sensitivity: Replacing k with r-k solves -Qprime, not Qprime; replacing b with -b without changing Qprime reverses the required scalar. Wrong inverse a^-1*b in recovery must be refused when it changes the scalar.
blinding_and_unblinding.truth_transport: H_P(Qprime)=H_r((b*a^-1*z) mod r). This generally differs from H_G(Q); blinding preserves subgroup and public solvability, not order/half-truth correlations.
blinding_and_unblinding.degenerate_inputs: a=0 collapses P and prevents inversion; b=0 makes Qprime=O. Reject each as outside the declared nonzero-unit domain.

interval_and_list_words.recurrence: For k_i=2^i*k mod r in [0,r-1], define b_i=floor(2*k_i/r), so k_(i+1)=2*k_i-b_i*r. For W=sum_{i=0}^{L-1} b_i*2^(L-1-i), k_L=2^L*k-r*W.
interval_and_list_words.exact_integer_interval: With D=2^L, lo=max(1,ceil(r*W/D)); hi=min(r-1,ceil(r*(W+1)/D)-1). Enumerate every integer lo<=k<=hi and apply public verification; empty lo>hi is retained.
interval_and_list_words.upper_guard: The upper guard is strict in the rational derivation. For odd r, gcd(r,D)=1 and 0<k<r, equality D*k=r*(W+1) cannot occur at an interior valid word boundary; < versus <= is then equivalent. Do not claim detection of an algebraically equivalent mutant. Dropping the upper guard can add false candidates and must be detected.
interval_and_list_words.uniqueness: If D>=r each word interval contains at most one integer because its real width r/D<=1 and its upper end is open. If D<r, all interval integers must be checked; a word does not itself certify a unique scalar.
interval_and_list_words.errors_and_erasures: For length L with e undefined positions and e<=erasure_cap, independently enumerate all 2^e completions and all flips of at most t among the L-e defined bits. Number of words=2^e*sum_{j=0}^{min(t,L-e)} C(L-e,j). If e>cap, preserve the rejected/ineligible result; do not impute labels.
interval_and_list_words.max_bound: For L<=17, e<=2 and t<=2, the maximum is 4*(1+15+105)=484 words. Candidate count M is the number of distinct canonical nonzero integers actually checked, not this word bound, not number of word checks, and not accepted-success count.
interval_and_list_words.duplicate_zero_and_failed_work: Different words may yield duplicate candidates or empty intervals; keep word count, generated candidates, duplicates, zero checks and distinct nonzero public checks separate. Enumeration continues after success when the frozen schedule requires it.

uniform_inclusion_law.population: N=r-1 canonical nonzero scalars, with a fixed legal target scalar z; K=min(M,N) for an integer nonnegative list budget M.
uniform_inclusion_law.assumption: The reference selects a uniform K-subset without replacement of this population. Rejection sampling is unbiased only conditional on uniform independent source draws; deterministic stream replay may check consistency but does not prove an ideal-hash randomness model.
uniform_inclusion_law.derivation: For 1<=K<=N, P(z included)=C(N-1,K-1)/C(N,K)=K/N. Equivalently each scalar has exchangeable inclusion indicator and the sum is K.

boundaries.M_0: K=0: empty set and inclusion probability 0.
boundaries.saturation: M>=N: K=N, every legal nonzero target included, probability 1.
boundaries.zero_target: z=0 excluded from this population; the K/N formula is inapplicable to an identity target.
boundaries.r_1: N=0 is outside declared odd-prime subgroup; no division by zero.

uniform_inclusion_law.duplicate_warning: Distinct canonical M<=N. Raw guesses with duplicates/zero do not create a uniform M-subset. Sampling with replacement would instead give 1-(1-1/N)^draws, a different law.
uniform_inclusion_law.interpretation: This conditional matched-M diagnostic inherits the work needed to determine M and is not a standalone solver. Six cell values may be correlated. Public equation success and label success must each be checked for every retained success and failure.

bsgs_decomposition_and_witness.width: Canonical width m=ceil(sqrt(r)); for nonsquare prime r, m=isqrt(r)+1. An explicitly declared alternative width can be algebraically checked, but is not silently called the canonical width.
bsgs_decomposition_and_witness.baby_table: B_j=[j]G for j=0,...,m-1 including B_0=O. For m<=r all m entries are distinct. Verify each retained entry or record the absent/incomplete witness coverage.
bsgs_decomposition_and_witness.giant_steps: For i=0,...,ceil(r/m)-1, T_i=Q-[i*m]G. A collision T_i=B_j yields raw z=i*m+j; require the exact declared range/reduction rule and [z mod r]G=Q.
bsgs_decomposition_and_witness.canonical_decomposition: Every 0<=z<r has unique i=floor(z/m), j=z mod m in these ranges. A canonical witness has z=i*m+j<r. If an implementation accepts a raw value >=r then its explicit modular reduction must be recorded and checked; the final canonical scalar still needs public verification.
bsgs_decomposition_and_witness.zero_boundary: For Q=O, i=j=0 gives z=0, but the scientific target domain excludes O. Do not treat O as a nonzero success or include it in matched-M budgets.
witness_checks: Curve parameters and primality/non-singularity; G exact order and Q subgroup membership.
Retained m matches declared width rule.
Each retained B_j equals own [j]G; each retained T_i equals own Q-[im]G, with exact indices.
Collision equality, raw decomposition and any reduction agree, and recovered scalar independently verifies.
All target IDs and failure rows covered; absence of a retained table/step/collision witness remains an explicit gap even if own log equality verifies the scalar.
bsgs_decomposition_and_witness.cost_limits: Table entry count, group equations and actual retained indices are finite logical facts. They do not independently certify actual producer event counters, physical memory, clock, or native instruction/field costs. Setup once per curve and online per target are distinct dimensions.

All retained cases covered or precise gap.
phase2_independent_arithmetic_plan.bsgs_coverage: Verify every retained scientific BSGS scalar plus every available retained table/step/decomposition/collision witness using own arithmetic. Missing internal witnesses or unexercised branches cannot be repaired by an own successful reconstruction.
phase2_independent_arithmetic_plan.mutations: Use tiny outside copies only: independently flip retained truth label, scalar sign/zero/alias, candidate budget duplicate count and BSGS index/width/collision/decomposition/canonical scalar/target. Refuse false certificates even when their metadata is mutually consistent; preserve the smallest rejected example.
phase2_independent_arithmetic_plan.scope: Zero scientific trials, new curves, targets, entropy, nonces, candidate/predicate queries, producer source execution, source reference calls, new scientific solver experiment or referencebank.
